title: Regulating Conflicts of Interest in Medicine Through Public Disclosure: Evidence from a Physician Payments Sunshine Law
eligible_reason: Single-policy DiD/DDD, not staggered adoption. Treatment sunshine_law = 1 for Massachusetts physicians from July 2009 (tm > 593), a single common date; control physicians are in four other states (NY, PA, IL, CA) and never treated. Main specifications (Tables 4-8, ChaoLarkin_Stata_Commands.do) are triple differences areg Rx1 sunshine_law##branded_no_generic i.tm, absorb(doc_drug) (and variants with Prescriber_ID FE, drug x month FE, product FE, and splits by prescriber volume, sales force, drug class); Table 5 uses the August 2008 signing date (again common); Figure 1 is an event study massdoc##branded##months_until_treatment. All treated units share one adoption date, so there is a single adoption cohort.
design_notes: Stata areg/reghdfe, physician x drug x month panel (Jul 2007-Jun 2011, 262 drugs, 5,730 physicians, five states), cluster university1 (AMC affiliation). Appendix Table A16 adds a staggered AMC-level own marketing policy (AMC_policy = 1 if AMC_Policy_tm <= tm) alongside sunshine_law, i.e., an extra treatment regressor in an appendix-only column.

ineligible_specs_listed.reason: single common adoption date (Massachusetts, July 2009 / Aug 2008 signing); DDD with branded-drug interaction
staggered AMC_policy entered alongside sunshine_law (extra treatment regressor), branded interactions; appendix only

data_files_note: readme.txt: prescriptions and affiliations from IMS Health (purchased), sales force data from SDI Health; only the Massachusetts disclosure data are public (archived web link). Package ships do-file, Stata output (docx) and a data dictionary; no data.
data_provenance_note: IMS Health proprietary data, contact given in README.
screener_notes: Screened from package and OpenAlex abstract (no article text, no PDF). Abstract confirms a 2009 Massachusetts quasi-experiment with control physicians in other states. Not a near-miss: one adoption cohort.
